chain.label: Fan blade dovetail peak stresses higher than originally predicted
chain.trigger: CFM reevaluated the fan blade dovetail stresses and found that the fatigue cracks initiated in an area of high stress on the dovetail and that the dovetail was experiencing peak stresses that were higher than originally predicted

chain.label: Low-cycle fatigue crack in dovetail of fan blade No. 13, initiated before the October 2012 overhaul
chain.trigger: Metallurgical examinations of the fractured fan blade found that the crack had likely initiated before the fan blade set's last overhaul in October 2012

caused_by.evidence: The low-cycle fatigue crack in the fan blade dovetail initiated because of higher-than-expected dovetail stresses under normal operating loads

chain.label: Overhaul FPI and on-wing visual inspections could not detect the dovetail crack
chain.trigger: the overhaul process included a fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI) to detect cracks; however, the crack was not detected for unknown reasons

caused_by.evidence: this crack was most likely not detectable during the fluorescent penetrant inspection at the time of the fan blade set's last overhaul and subsequent visual inspections at the time of fan blade relubrications

chain.label: Certification did not account for critical fan blade impact locations or the radial restraint fitting load path
chain.trigger: FBO-generated loads were transmitted to the fan cowl through the radial restraint fitting, which was not accounted for in the fan cowl's design, and the stresses in the fan cowl were greater than those calculated in the certification analyses

chain.label: Fan blade No. 13 fractured at its root in flight and impacted the fan case near the six o'clock position
chain.trigger: the No. 1 (left) engine's fan and core speeds decreased, and the engine's vibration parameters increased... The separated fan blade impacted the engine fan case near the six o'clock position and fractured into multiple fragments

caused_by.evidence: a low-cycle fatigue crack in the dovetail of fan blade No. 13, which resulted in the fan blade separating in flight and impacting the engine fan case at a location that was critical to the structural integrity and performance of the fan cowl structure
The crack on the fan blade involved in the PHL accident was also not detected during the on-wing fan blade visual inspections

chain.label: Inlet structure compromised by forward-traveling blade fragments and displacement wave; portions of inlet departed
chain.trigger: The forward-traveling fan blade fragments and the deformation compromised the structural integrity of the inlet, causing portions of the inlet to depart the airplane

caused_by.evidence: Some of the fan blade fragments traveled forward of the engine and into the inlet... the fan blade's impact with the fan case caused the fan case to deform locally

chain.label: Fan cowl cracked at the radial restraint fitting, latches severed, and fan cowl halves separated and departed
chain.trigger: These loads caused cracks to form in the fan cowl skin and frames near the radial restraint fitting. This damage then propagated forward and aft, severing the three latch assemblies... which caused large portions of both fan cowl halves to separate and depart the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the impact of the separated fan blade with the fan case imparted significant loads into the fan cowl through the radial restraint fitting
the associated stresses in the fan cowl structure exceeded the residual strength of the fan cowl, causing its failure

chain.label: Aft latch keeper struck fuselage, cabin window at seat 14A departed, cabin rapidly depressurized
chain.trigger: One fan cowl fragment impacted the left-side fuselage near a cabin window, and the window departed the airplane, which resulted in a rapid depressurization

caused_by.evidence: The impact of the inboard fan cowl aft latch keeper with the fuselage near the cabin window adjacent to seat 14A caused the window to depart the airplane, the rapid depressurization of the cabin, and the passenger fatality

chain.label: Passenger in seat 14A partially pulled through the window opening and fatally injured; 8 minor injuries
chain.trigger: the head, upper torso, and arms of the passenger seated in 14A had been pulled outside the airplane through the window... 1 passenger received fatal injuries, and 8 passengers received minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: the passenger's cause of death was 'blunt force trauma of the head, neck, and torso.' These injuries were not survivable

chain.label: Emergency descent and single-engine diversion to Philadelphia; airplane landed safely but was substantially damaged
chain.trigger: the flight crew conducted an emergency descent and diverted to Philadelphia International Airport (PHL)... The airplane landed safely at PHL about 17 minutes after the engine failure occurred

caused_by.evidence: As a result of the engine failure, the flight crew conducted an emergency descent and diverted to Philadelphia International Airport
fragments from the inlet and fan cowl struck the left wing, the left-side fuselage, and the left horizontal stabilizer
the captain stated that, although she had requested a long final approach, she decided to expedite the approach... when she learned about the injured passenger
